stemMd: Which statement distinguishes a strong acid from a concentrated acid?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Strength concerns ionization in water; concentration concerns amount per volume.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Concentration measures only the number of protons in an atomic nucleus.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Every dilute acid must be weak.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Every concentrated acid must be strong.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Strength is simply the colour of the solution.

explanationMd: Acid strength describes the tendency to donate protons, commonly expressed by an equilibrium constant or extent of ionization. Concentration describes how much acid is present in a given amount of solution. These are separate properties, so strong acids can be dilute and weak acids concentrated.

distractorRationale.d: A weak acid can be present at high concentration.
distractorRationale.c: A strong acid can be diluted.
distractorRationale.e: Colour does not define acid strength.
distractorRationale.b: Solution concentration concerns amount of solute relative to volume or another measure.
